message.content:
In the repository at /private/tmp/live-spec-integrate-slimdown/wt, I need to find the DOCUMENTED procedure ("the send road" / push road) for what a worker does when the pre-push guard (guardrails/pre-push) reds on the class of "machine-local" failures — specifically:

1. gate m / config-health (`guardrails/check-config-health.sh`) failing with "installed skill drifted from source" (a mismatch between repo `skills/<name>/` and the installed `~/.claude/skills/<name>`), and
2. gate b / the test suite failing only on `tests/test_worker_restore.py::TestTheGateIsArmedWhereItSaysItIs::test_the_gate_runs_against_this_machines_own_transcripts` (a gate that scans the machine's own Claude transcripts for destructive git commands).

I need to know whether there is a WRITTEN, documented path for pushing anyway in that situation, and exactly what it says. Look for:
- Any documented use of `--no-verify`, an env var carve-out (e.g. `LIVE_SPEC_*` variables the pre-push script honours), a "declared local override" mechanism (I saw `guardrails/local-overrides.json` mentioned in check-config-health.sh), or an owner-word exemption.
- The push/send procedure documentation: search skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md, skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md and their references/, PRODUCT_SPEC.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/ (especially anything named like push, send, release, landing, road), guardrails/README.md, ROADMAP.md, .live-spec/PROBLEMS.md, JOURNAL.md.
- Whether `scripts/sync-skills.sh` is documented as the prerequisite step BEFORE a push (i.e. the drift must be cleared first rather than bypassed).
- Read guardrails/pre-push in full and report every environment variable or condition that makes it stand down, skip a gate, or exit early.

Report precisely: quote the relevant lines with file paths and line numbers. If there is NO documented bypass for this class, say so clearly and explicitly — do not infer or invent one. Distinguish sharply between (a) something actually written down as a procedure, and (b) something you merely deduce is technically possible.

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pre-push — the live-spec push gate (SPEC M-6; scope grown by prover findings F7/F4;
# gate e added for INV-17, the prototype fence).
# Blocks a push unless every gate below passes.
#
# Generic pattern for a host project: copy this file, then in guardrails/README.md's
# "how a host adapts" section swap in your own test command and prover cadence — the
# gate shape (fresh review record / green tests / ownership / coverage) travels as-is.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"
GUARDRAILS="$REPO_ROOT/guardrails"

# -- deletion-only stand-down (SPEC INV-290, ROADMAP row 502) --
# git feeds this hook one ref-update line per pushed ref on stdin (githooks(5)); read it ONCE, here,
# before any gate below can touch stdin — a manual invocation for testing leaves stdin as a tty and
# must never block on a read. A push whose every fed line deletes its remote counterpart (the
# all-zero local object id) carries no content for any gate to judge, so the whole chain stands down
# by name instead of falling to the reach map's conservative FULL — the fix for the 2026-07-27 hang
# (four tag deletions read as an empty diff, fell to the full suite, died on the two-minute limit).
# This check carries no gate letter: it is a triage read ahead of the chain, the placement
# check-push-reach.sh already holds inside gate b, not a net that blocks on red.
#
# The marker below is the machine-readable half of the convention guardrails/check-prover-record.sh
# states in full: every arm that can let a push past the prover-record demand carries one
# `# STAND-DOWN: <name>` line, and PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226 criterion 6 must name that same <name>.
# tests/test_deletion_only_push.py reads both directions off these markers.
# STAND-DOWN: deletion-only
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  PUSH_REF_LINES=""
else
  PUSH_REF_LINES="$(cat)"
fi
export PUSH_REF_LINES
if [ -n "$PUSH_REF_LINES" ]; then
  set +e
  del_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-deletion-only-push.sh")"
  del_code=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$del_code" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "$del_out"
    echo "PUSH ALLOWED — deletion-only push: standing the full gate chain down (reason: a deletion carries no content for any gate to judge, SPEC INV-290); whatever would guard the deletion itself is unaffected, since no such gate exists in this chain today."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

fail=0

echo "== live-spec push gate =="

echo ""
echo "-- reach classification (one read, feeds gates a and b, SPEC INV-45) --"
set +e
reach_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-push-reach.sh")"
reach_code=$?
set -e
echo "$reach_out"

echo ""
echo "-- gate a: fresh prover record for today (one record per push: the re-check of the spec and the architecture, and the adversarial read of the pushed range, SPEC M-6/INV-116/INV-304) --"
# The reach verdict does not scope this gate (the 2718c69 stand-down, reverted on the owner's
# 2026-08-15 word). A prose-only or scoped diff still sends commits, and the record this gate
# demands is the adversarial read of the pushed RANGE (INV-304) — a thing no file-class verdict
# can stand down for. The only stand-downs that exist are the two PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226.6 names
# by hand: a deletion-only push (handled above, before this chain) and the recordless class.
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-prover-record.sh" --push; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate b: test suite green (scoped by the diff's reach, SPEC INV-45) --"
case "$reach_code" in
  0)
    echo "   prose-only diff: the suite stands down by name; every other gate still runs."
    ;;
  2)
    scoped_files="$(printf '%s\n' "$reach_out" | sed -n 's/^SCOPED //p')"
    if ! SCOPED_TEST_FILES="$scoped_files" "$GUARDRAILS/check-tests.sh"; then
      fail=1
    fi
    ;;
  *)
    if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-tests.sh"; then
      fail=1
    fi
    ;;
esac

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# check-config-health.sh — the installed gate is the source gate (SPEC INV-175).
     3	#
     4	# A gate lives twice: its source in guardrails/ travels with the repo; its installed copy in
     5	# .git/hooks/ actually runs. They drift the moment an install is skipped — the worked instance
     6	# (2026-07-16): the installed pre-push was missing gates k and l that the source carried.
     7	# This check reds when an expected hook is missing from .git/hooks/ or differs byte-for-byte
     8	# from its guardrails/ source, and names the one fix. A checkout with no installed hooks by
     9	# design (CI) skips by name. Runs inside the suite, so even a stale pre-push that still runs
    10	# the tests surfaces the drift — the self-healing shape.
    11	
    12	set -euo pipefail
    13	
    14	if [ "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}" = "true" ] || [ "${CI:-}" = "true" ]; then
    15	  echo "config-health: skip (CI checkout installs no local hooks by design)"
    16	  exit 0
    17	fi
    18	
    19	REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
    20	HOOKS_DIR="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --git-path hooks)"
    21	case "$HOOKS_DIR" in
    22	  /*) : ;;
    23	  *) HOOKS_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/$HOOKS_DIR" ;;
    24	esac
    25	
    26	fail=0
    27	for name in pre-commit pre-push; do
    28	  src="$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/$name"
    29	  [ -f "$src" ] || continue
    30	  inst="$HOOKS_DIR/$name"
    31	  if [ ! -f "$inst" ]; then
    32	    echo "{\"severity\":\"error\",\"code\":\"config-health\",\"message\":\"installed hook missing: .git/hooks/$name\",\"fix\":\"run guardrails/install.sh\"}"
    33	    fail=1
    34	  elif ! cmp -s "$src" "$inst"; then
    35	    echo "{\"severity\":\"error\",\"code\":\"config-health\",\"message\":\"installed hook drifted from source: $name\",\"fix\":\"run guardrails/install.sh\"}"
    36	    fail=1
    37	  fi
    38	done
    39	
    40	# INV-173 x INV-175 (batch audit 2026-07-16, F3; inverted ROADMAP 417): the pack's session hooks are
    41	# gates living twice too. Rather than a hardcoded basename list — which goes blind to every hook added
    42	# after it was written (it was blind to hook-meter.py and the register-judge arms installed 2026-07-17)
    43	# — DIFF the whole hook SOURCE directory (hooks/) against the installed set. Every file in hooks/ is
    44	# covered automatically: when an installed copy exists it must match its source byte-for-byte; when a
    45	# source hook has NO installed copy that is drift and it reds (source exists, install missing = the
    46	# config is unhealthy, and a missing installed judge goes dark while every other gate stays green —
    47	# corrected 2026-07-17, the earlier form skipped a missing install green). A file living only in the
    48	# installed set (a personal-layer overlay the pack never ships) has no source here and is correctly left
    49	# alone. RESIDUAL for row 420's gate audit: this arm proves the installed FILE exists and matches; it
    50	# does not yet prove settings.json still LISTS the Stop/UserPromptSubmit judge entries — that check is
    51	# harder because settings.json is personal-layer, and it is left for the row 420 gate audit.
    52	HOOK_SRC_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/hooks"
    53	if [ -d "$HOOK_SRC_DIR" ]; then
    54	  for src_hook in "$HOOK_SRC_DIR"/*; do
    55	    [ -f "$src_hook" ] || continue
    56	    hname="$(basename "$src_hook")"
    57	    inst_hook="$HOME/.claude/hooks/$hname"
    58	    if [ ! -f "$inst_hook" ]; then
    59	      echo "{\"severity\":\"error\",\"code\":\"config-health\",\"message\":\"installed hook missing: ~/.claude/hooks/$hname (source exists, install missing)\",\"fix\":\"run scripts/install-pack-hooks.sh or scripts/install-session-hooks.sh\"}"
    60	      fail=1
    61	    elif ! cmp -s "$src_hook" "$inst_hook"; then
    62	      # A machine may deliberately run a changed copy of a hook — a check switched off for a stated
    63	      # span while the documents it reads are rewritten, say. The repository stays the version
    64	      # everyone gets, and the difference is declared as DATA in guardrails/local-overrides.json
    65	      # rather than by editing this script. An entry pins the fingerprint of the installed file it
    66	      # covers, so it buys silence for exactly that copy: change the installed file again and the
    67	      # entry stops matching and this arm reds. An undeclared difference still reds (2026-08-04).
    68	      inst_sha="$(shasum -a 256 "$inst_hook" | awk '{print $1}')"
    69	      if [ -f "$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/local-overrides.json" ] && python3 - "$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/local-overrides.json" "$hname" "$inst_sha" <<'PYCHECK'
    70	import json, sys
    71	path, hook, sha = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
    72	try:
    73	    entries = json.load(open(path, encoding="utf-8")).get("hook_overrides", [])
    74	except Exception:
    75	    sys.exit(1)
    76	for e in entries:
    77	    if e.get("hook") == hook and e.get("installed_sha256") == sha and e.get("reason"):
    78	        sys.exit(0)
    79	sys.exit(1)
    80	PYCHECK
    81	      then
    82	        echo "config-health: declared local override, installed hook differs from source by design: $hname (guardrails/local-overrides.json)"
    83	      else
    84	        echo "{\"severity\":\"error\",\"code\":\"config-health\",\"message\":\"installed hook drifted from source: $hname\",\"fix\":\"run scripts/install-pack-hooks.sh or scripts/install-session-hooks.sh, or declare the difference in guardrails/local-overrides.json with its reason and the installed file's fingerprint\"}"
    85	        fail=1
    86	      fi
    87	    fi
    88	  done
    89	fi
    90	
    91	# INV-243: a skill is a gate living twice too — source in skills/ travels with the repo, the
    92	# installed copy under ~/.claude/skills/<name> is what a pack skill actually loads from. Same
    93	# shape as the session-hook directory-diff arm above, but the unit is a whole DIRECTORY TREE (a
    94	# skill carries SKILL.md plus references/, scripts/...), so the compare is a recursive tree diff
    95	# rather than a single-file cmp. A WHOLE skill installed under ~/.claude/skills with no pack source
    96	# (a personal-layer skill the pack never ships) is never iterated here and is correctly left alone —
    97	# the same TOP-LEVEL asymmetry the hook arm holds. A shipped skill's installed copy is held
    98	# byte-pristine, though: because the compare is a recursive tree diff, an extra file dropped INSIDE a
    99	# shipped skill's directory counts as drift and reds. That is stricter than the hook arm's flat-file
   100	# tolerance, and intended — a shipped skill should match its source tree exactly.
   101	SKILL_SRC_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/skills"
   102	if [ -d "$SKILL_SRC_DIR" ]; then
   103	  for src_skill in "$SKILL_SRC_DIR"/*/; do
   104	    [ -d "$src_skill" ] || continue
   105	    sname="$(basename "$src_skill")"
   106	    # External-skill fence (shared policy; siblings: install.sh, scripts/sync-skills.sh,
   107	    # scripts/sync-mirrors.sh): a skill dir holding its own .git is the external canonical clone —
   108	    # scripts/install-external-skills.sh owns its installed copy, not the sync; INV-243 holds
   109	    # pack-owned skills only.
   110	    if [ -e "$src_skill/.git" ]; then
   111	      continue
   112	    fi
   113	    inst_skill="$HOME/.claude/skills/$sname"
   114	    if [ ! -d "$inst_skill" ]; then
   115	      echo "{\"severity\":\"error\",\"code\":\"config-health\",\"message\":\"installed skill missing: ~/.claude/skills/$sname (source exists, install missing)\",\"fix\":\"run scripts/sync-skills.sh\"}"
   116	      fail=1
   117	    elif ! diff -rq "$src_skill" "$inst_skill" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   118	      echo "{\"severity\":\"error\",\"code\":\"config-health\",\"message\":\"installed skill drifted from source: $sname\",\"fix\":\"run scripts/sync-skills.sh\"}"
   119	      fail=1
   120	    fi
   121	  done
   122	fi
   123	
   124	# INV-216: a permission rule that points at nothing is a dead rule. This arm reads every permission
   125	# rule that names a filesystem path in the personal ~/.claude/settings.json and the host's project
   126	# settings and reds a rule whose path is absent — the ~/tlvphoto→~/tlvphotos rename (2026-07-10) sat
   127	# a week failing silently into prompts. Personal-layer: it stands down by name where the settings
   128	# cannot be read and never falsely passes. Rides gate m's existing CI carve-out (a CI checkout skips
   129	# this whole script) and gate m's red proof; it adds no gate letter.
   130	PERMS="$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/check-config-health-perms.py"
   131	if [ -f "$PERMS" ]; then
   132	  if ! python3 "$PERMS"; then
   133	    fail=1
   134	  fi
   135	fi
   136	
   137	if [ "$fail" -eq 0 ]; then
   138	  echo "config-health: OK (installed hooks match their sources)"
   139	fi
   140	exit "$fail"

=== PUSH-LAW ===
     1	# Commit and push gates
     2	
     3	This page explains what stands between a finished change and the remote: the done-gate a gated file
     4	passes before any commit, the rule that decides when a commit happens, the law that moves accepted
     5	work to the remote, how a delegated run's verdict is read, and the tighter gates a host may add.
     6	Each rule's normative home is linked; this page explains and points, and the homes decide.
     7	
     8	## The done-gate before a commit
     9	
    10	`scripts/spec-done-gate.py` is the single definition of "done" for a gated prose file
    11	(the design lives in `docs/prose-quality-gate-design.md`). The script runs a conjunction of
    12	checks and prints green only when all of them hold. Exit 0 means green; exit 1 means red, and a
    13	red gate blocks the commit. The conditions are:
    14	
    15	- `spec-style-lint.py --gate` reports zero errors on the file. In gate mode the two advisory
    16	  signals (caps-shout, second-person) become blocking errors, and a dated waiver file can move a
    17	  still-unfixed finding into a counted debt bucket. A waiver is a recorded, visible debt; a silent
    18	  pass never happens.
    19	- `spec-redundancy-precheck.py` reports zero open findings; each finding is either resolved or
    20	  waived.
    21	- The prose judge, a language-model check, has passed its self-test and left zero surviving
    22	  definite or likely findings.
    23	  The judge's output file is required; without it the gate is red with "judge pending".
    24	- The anchor multiset of the file is unchanged against a given git baseline. An anchor is a
    25	  trailing code in brackets, such as `[INV-82]`; the multiset check proves a prose restyle moved
    26	  no normative pointer.
    27	
    28	Suite green is a separate leg of the same commit bar. The test suite, the needle tests, waiver
    29	hygiene, and the debt ratchet run as pytest classes under `tests/`. A commit waits for both legs:
    30	the done-gate on the gated files and a green suite.
    31	
    32	## The commit rule
    33	
    34	A change is committed when it leaves the tree the same or better. Green with no regression is
    35	enough; the pipeline never parks finished work while waiting for perfect
    36	(`skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md`, step 9). Before the commit, every check the diff can reach has
    37	run: a prose-only diff reaches the prose gates, a code diff reaches the suite (SPEC INV-45).
    38	
    39	## The push law
    40	
    41	Accepted work reaches the project's remote by rule (SPEC INV-82; the normative text lives in
    42	`PRODUCT_SPEC.md`). "Accepted" means the change is same or better and every gate the diff reaches
    43	ran and passed. The law has four parts:
    44	
    45	- **Push by rule.** Where the host has a remote, accepted work is pushed. Parking it locally
    46	  while waiting for a perfect state breaks the law.
    47	- **Discover the remote first.** The remote is read from the tree; `git remote -v` already
    48	  answers the question, so the agent never asks it.
    49	- **One question when no remote exists.** A host with no remote gets a single contextual question
    50	  at the first push moment: create a remote (and where — GitHub, GitLab, whatever the human
    51	  names) or stay local. The answer is recorded in the host profile and the question never
    52	  repeats.
    53	- **Re-walk the README at every push.** Every push checks the README against the pushed truth:
    54	  claims, counts, commands, and version homes still match, and a stale claim is fixed before the
    55	  push. This is the shopfront law at every-push cadence (SPEC INV-44).
    56	
    57	A push that changes what a public reader sees also passes the publish-quality gate first: the
    58	publication owes its reader what the artifact's kind owes, such as fresh screenshots for a visual
    59	product or real runs for a tool (`skills/publish/SKILL.md`). The publish gate prepares the
    60	deposit; it never turns into a push authorization on its own.
    61	
    62	## Reading a delegated run's verdict
    63	
    64	A wrapper's exit code reports the wrapper, so for a background or delegated run it is never the
    65	verdict. A background job can exit 0 while the suite inside it failed. The gate therefore reads
    66	the suite log's own tail line — the "N/N green" line the suite itself prints — and that line is
    67	the verdict (SPEC INV-80). A foreground gate reading the exit code of its own direct child stays
    68	legal, because there the exit code is the suite's own.
    69	
    70	## Host-level tighter gates
    71	
    72	The rules above are the package floor. A host or a human may tighten them; loosening a gate takes
    73	a recorded profile entry, never a silent skip (`skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md`, the settings
    74	ladder).

=== PUSH-LAW ===
     1	# Commit and push gates
     2	
     3	This page explains what stands between a finished change and the remote: the done-gate a gated file
     4	passes before any commit, the rule that decides when a commit happens, the law that moves accepted
     5	work to the remote, how a delegated run's verdict is read, and the tighter gates a host may add.
     6	Each rule's normative home is linked; this page explains and points, and the homes decide.
     7	
     8	## The done-gate before a commit
     9	
    10	`scripts/spec-done-gate.py` is the single definition of "done" for a gated prose file
    11	(the design lives in `docs/prose-quality-gate-design.md`). The script runs a conjunction of
    12	checks and prints green only when all of them hold. Exit 0 means green; exit 1 means red, and a
    13	red gate blocks the commit. The conditions are:
    14	
    15	- `spec-style-lint.py --gate` reports zero errors on the file. In gate mode the two advisory
    16	  signals (caps-shout, second-person) become blocking errors, and a dated waiver file can move a
    17	  still-unfixed finding into a counted debt bucket. A waiver is a recorded, visible debt; a silent
    18	  pass never happens.
    19	- `spec-redundancy-precheck.py` reports zero open findings; each finding is either resolved or
    20	  waived.
    21	- The prose judge, a language-model check, has passed its self-test and left zero surviving
    22	  definite or likely findings.
    23	  The judge's output file is required; without it the gate is red with "judge pending".
    24	- The anchor multiset of the file is unchanged against a given git baseline. An anchor is a
    25	  trailing code in brackets, such as `[INV-82]`; the multiset check proves a prose restyle moved
    26	  no normative pointer.
    27	
    28	Suite green is a separate leg of the same commit bar. The test suite, the needle tests, waiver
    29	hygiene, and the debt ratchet run as pytest classes under `tests/`. A commit waits for both legs:
    30	the done-gate on the gated files and a green suite.
    31	
    32	## The commit rule
    33	
    34	A change is committed when it leaves the tree the same or better. Green with no regression is
    35	enough; the pipeline never parks finished work while waiting for perfect
    36	(`skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md`, step 9). Before the commit, every check the diff can reach has
    37	run: a prose-only diff reaches the prose gates, a code diff reaches the suite (SPEC INV-45).
    38	
    39	## The push law
    40	
    41	Accepted work reaches the project's remote by rule (SPEC INV-82; the normative text lives in
    42	`PRODUCT_SPEC.md`). "Accepted" means the change is same or better and every gate the diff reaches
    43	ran and passed. The law has four parts:
    44	
    45	- **Push by rule.** Where the host has a remote, accepted work is pushed. Parking it locally
    46	  while waiting for a perfect state breaks the law.
    47	- **Discover the remote first.** The remote is read from the tree; `git remote -v` already
    48	  answers the question, so the agent never asks it.
    49	- **One question when no remote exists.** A host with no remote gets a single contextual question
    50	  at the first push moment: create a remote (and where — GitHub, GitLab, whatever the human
    51	  names) or stay local. The answer is recorded in the host profile and the question never
    52	  repeats.
    53	- **Re-walk the README at every push.** Every push checks the README against the pushed truth:
    54	  claims, counts, commands, and version homes still match, and a stale claim is fixed before the
    55	  push. This is the shopfront law at every-push cadence (SPEC INV-44).
    56	
    57	A push that changes what a public reader sees also passes the publish-quality gate first: the
    58	publication owes its reader what the artifact's kind owes, such as fresh screenshots for a visual
    59	product or real runs for a tool (`skills/publish/SKILL.md`). The publish gate prepares the
    60	deposit; it never turns into a push authorization on its own.
    61	
    62	## Reading a delegated run's verdict
    63	
    64	A wrapper's exit code reports the wrapper, so for a background or delegated run it is never the
    65	verdict. A background job can exit 0 while the suite inside it failed. The gate therefore reads
    66	the suite log's own tail line — the "N/N green" line the suite itself prints — and that line is
    67	the verdict (SPEC INV-80). A foreground gate reading the exit code of its own direct child stays
    68	legal, because there the exit code is the suite's own.

613:class TestTheGateIsArmedWhereItSaysItIs:
614:    """The gate declares itself blocking at the verify step, and this is where that is proven.
615:
616:    Two arms. The pipeline skill's verify step names the command a session runs before it accepts a
617:    worker's result. This suite runs the same gate against the machine's own transcript root, so a
618:    red reaches a person on the next suite run rather than sitting on disk.
619:    """

622:        skill = read_flat("skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md")
623:        assert "python3 guardrails/check-worker-restore.py" in skill, (

ROADMAP.md:203:| 527 | **A completed recovery leaves the worker-command check red for a day, and nothing clears it** (found 2026-07-29 when a worker ran a command that discards uncommitted work): `guardrails/check-worker-restore.py` reads the worker runs' own records and reds on a command that discards uncommitted work. The record of that run stays on disk, so the finding stays true forever, and the suite arm reads a window of 24 hours. content.content:
1:#!/usr/bin/env bash
2:# sync-skills.sh — the pack developer's freshness tool (SPEC E-23).
3:# Copies each repo skill over its installed copy and REPORTS every version change old -> new,
4:# so the A-7 re-read has its trigger line. The repo is the source (D-4); the installed copy
5:# is a mirror that must never run stale through a working session.
6:# Usage: scripts/sync-skills.sh [dest]   (default: ~/.claude/skills)
7:
8:set -euo pipefail
9:
10:REPO_SKILLS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../skills" && pwd)"
11:DEST="${1:-$HOME/.claude/skills}"
12:
13:mkdir -p "$DEST"
14:
15:version_of() {
16:  # frontmatter form:  metadata:\n  version: X.Y.Z
17:  awk '/^  version: / { print $2; exit }' "$1" 2>/dev/null || true
18:}
19:
20:changed=0
21:for skill_dir in "$REPO_SKILLS"/*/; do
22:  name="$(basename "$skill_dir")"
23:  # External-skill fence — the shared policy install.sh and scripts/sync-mirrors.sh already carry:
24:  # a skill dir holding its own .git is the external canonical clone; never copy it (or its .git).
25:  if [ -e "$skill_dir/.git" ]; then
26:    echo "  $name — SKIPPED (external skill's canonical clone; scripts/install-external-skills.sh owns it)"
27:    continue
28:  fi
29:  src_v="$(version_of "$skill_dir/SKILL.md")"
30:  dst_v="$(version_of "$DEST/$name/SKILL.md")"
31:  # Skip only when the installed tree is byte-identical to the source — the SAME whole-tree compare
32:  # the config-health skill-copy arm reds on (INV-243). Gating the skip on the SKILL.md version or
33:  # mtime alone let a drift confined to a non-SKILL.md file (a reference edited with no version bump)
34:  # red the gate while re-running this fix skipped it as "unchanged" — a red with no working escape.
35:  if [ -d "$DEST/$name" ] && diff -rq "$skill_dir" "$DEST/$name" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
36:    echo "  $name — unchanged ($src_v)"
37:    continue
38:  fi
39:  mkdir -p "$DEST/$name"
40:  cp -r "$skill_dir"/. "$DEST/$name/"
=== who names sync-skills as pre-push step ===

394:The two remaining stories were deterministic gates, so they routed as an infra build: a reader distilled the target surfaces, the orchestrator authored the law text and the exact insert strings, and three workers ran in parallel on disjoint files — the docs (spec + architecture + matrix), the landing gate, and the config-health arm. INV-243 earned its keep on the first run: it caught that all ten installed skills on the machine had drifted to 2.8.1 while the pack source was at 3.0.0, and they were re-synced. The full minor gate then ran three fresh-seat judgment passes concurrently — a FULL prover, a design review of the two same-kind groups (the suite-riding checks and the config-health arms), and an adversarial audit that built throwaway repos to break both gates.
396:The three passes earned their cost. The design review found the real one: the landing gate declared itself suite-riding for the reason its chat-surface siblings use — "no committed file to scan" — which is false for a commit-range check, and the consequence was that its law was enforced nowhere on the real tree, fixtures only. Folded by correcting the reason (the push-gate letters are exhausted, so it rides gate b, which still blocks the push) and adding a live-tree test that runs the check over the repo's own commit range. The prover found the named fix could fail to clear its own red: `sync-skills.sh` re-copied only on a SKILL.md version or mtime change, so a drift in a non-SKILL.md file stayed red with no working escape — folded so the fix re-copies on any tree difference, the same whole-tree compare the gate reds on. The adversarial audit confirmed neither gate was hollow (every real-shaped drift reds) and surfaced a latent parser fragility — a fixed column index let an escaped pipe in a wish cell hide a landing — folded by splitting on unescaped pipes only, red-first proven against the real ROADMAP vocabulary (the status token `landed` is not always bolded, so a bold-only rule was rejected for its 27 false negatives). The design review's skill-arm note (a recursive tree diff holds a shipped skill byte-pristine, stricter than the flat-file hook arm) was folded as a precise spec-and-comment correction rather than a behaviour change, since byte-pristine is the intended contract. The executable-bit-only drift the audit found is a nit with no live exposure, queued far (ROADMAP 435). One known duplication stays unfolded: the commit-range base ladder now lives in three files, but two are shell and one is Python, so no shared helper extracts — the first Python instance, noted here, a compaction row on its second.
458:re-synced so config-health reads no drift.
518:The first live exercise of the lane-open act (INV-214): three independent rows ran at once, each in its own isolated worktree, then integrated onto main in a declared order. Row 379 states that a prose paragraph packing an enumeration of three or more parallel facts earns bullet structure (INV-215, M-396). Row 406 gives config-health an arm that reds a permission rule whose filesystem path no longer exists (INV-216, M-397). Row 407 states the release-tier rule — a version's number answers what taking the release costs a host, minor, major, or patch (INV-217, M-398). The three were disjoint in intent, and all three landed their prose on the same shared documents, which is where the integration work sat.
572:Then the same inversion across four gates, each a list becoming a check that reads what a thing IS: **INV-162** (`check-broad-kill.sh`) reds any ending that names a name — `pkill`/`killall`, or `kill` fed by a `pgrep`/`pidof` lookup — and accepts an owned PID / process group / owned path, the browser words demoted to the error's explanation; the probe corpus is a committed fixture (`tests/fixtures/kill_probes.txt`) so a later widening cannot silently narrow it, and `killall Safari`, `pkill -f node`, `killall -9 Electron`, `pkill firefox`, `pkill -f Slack` all red beside bare `pkill chrome`. **INV-120** (`check-shipped-language.py`) reads a declared alphabet held as allowlist data, so the detector's own source names no person and a collaborator's name is one data line. **INV-175** (`check-config-health.sh`) diffs the whole hook source directory against the installed set, covering register-judge*.sh and any future hook automatically, where the three-name loop went blind. **INV-152** (`check-deferral-marker.py`) reads the grammatical shape of a deferral, so `⟨DECIDE⟩` — the marker policing open decisions — is itself caught when it names no reason.
807:writes its one file and stops — the commit road raced the shared index. Config-health: the installed
829:committing, as its own step. CI failed once after the release push: the config-health temp-repo
874:  (№1), retroactive migration (№4), config-health gate, and the turnkey freeze-at-current-size adoption
1736:`guardrails/` rather than under `hooks/` also keeps config-health (gate m) and judge-listed (gate v)
1903:Five test cases added; installed judge copies re-synced so config-health reads no drift. Pushed and deployed.
1934:4.0.0 → 4.0.1 after the version stamp (config-health's own red pointed at it, sync-skills run, all
2226:sync-skills cleared three drifted installed copies: build-pipeline, spec-author and text-audit, each

3293:**Context:** The publish skill owns the per-kind checklist, and this spec sets the contract it follows. Nothing is deposited outward without passing the checklist first, and its result rides the delivery report. The map is conservative: anything it cannot classify falls to the full run.

5639:1. *when* a stopping point is reached, the system *shall* report a descendant that is owned, orphaned, and burning — its identity, its processor share, and why the run owns it — reasoning over process group, parent liveness, and processor share alone, and *shall* fire this notice at the stopping point and never at the push gate, which runs long after the cores burn. 5875:**User Story:** As a maintainer trusting the push gate, I want the gate machinery itself checked, so that no gate silently protects nothing — mirrored into the remote, wired into settings, provably able to fail, and pointed at real paths.
5881:1. *when* the push gate runs a gate letter locally that the remote mirror does not run, the system *shall* red, naming the gate and the one fix, a legitimate remote-skip living in `guardrails/ci-mirror.json` with its reason. [INV-210, M-5]
5981:**Context:** The pack runs on its own method, and its repository is a shared surface whose push gates run mechanically on installed hooks. Only a session assigned to the pack itself writes this repository; every other session is read-only here, with one exception — creating a new file in the inbox. A developer's machine keeps its installed skills fresh by a named step, since a hand-copy syncs silently and tells the next breakpoint nothing.
5996:5. The system *shall* run the repository's own push gates mechanically on installed hooks — a fresh prover record, a green suite, anchor ownership, and matrix coverage. [M-4]
6077:8. *when* the pack repository runs its monitor, the system *shall* run it as a scheduled action pushing inbox commits only under a single-instance concurrency group, riding the inbox-only carve-out the push gate already grants. [INV-148, M-6]

The config-health check reds the drift and names the one fix, and it runs inside the suite so even a stale push gate that still runs the tests surfaces the drift.
6513:1. *when* an expected hook is missing from the hooks directory or differs from its source, the system *shall* red the config-health check and name the one fix, running it inside the suite and wiring it into the push gate itself. [INV-175, INV-164]
7461:**Context:** This requirement and the push gate's own re-check asked one push for two review records, written into two homes and read by two checks, over one and the same change. Both are one adversarial pass over one delta, so they are now one record: Requirement 141 carries the whole duty, and the record lives with every other review record under `docs/prover/`. The merge is recorded in DECISIONS.md. The adversarial read itself is untouched — only the second record and the second check are gone.
7476:**Context:** A reader who meets a number decides whether to trust it. A count a person typed goes stale as the tree grows. The reader cannot tell a fresh count from a stale one. So every count this repository publishes about its own tree carries a declared measurement, a home, and a push gate.

5402:## Requirement 226: The push gate derives its reach from the diff
5403:
5404:**Context:** Running every check before every push double-misses: a prose-only push pays for behavioural tests that read none of its changed lines, while the checks a prose diff can break never run. So the push gate derives its check-set from a declared reach map — which checks read which file classes — read mechanically from the diff's file list. The map is conservative: anything it cannot classify falls to the full run.
5405:
5406:**User Story:** As a maintainer pushing a change, I want the gate to run every check the diff can reach and only those, so that a prose push stands down the behavioural suite by name while an unclassified file still pulls the whole run.
5407:
5408:### Acceptance Criteria
5409:
5410:**Case: the reach map decides the set**
5411:
5412:1. *when* a push runs, the system *shall* derive its check-set from the declared reach map against the diff's file list, and *shall* run the full suite *if* any changed file is unmapped or new. [INV-45, INV-40]
5413:2. *when* a diff is confined to the declared infra classes, the system *shall* run the test files that read its changed files plus the traceability net, and *shall* log the picked set with its reason. [INV-45, INV-212, INV-18]
5414:   - the traceability net is the suite's own traceability tests, carrying the anchor-ownership assertion and riding every scoped run, a mechanism distinct from the feature-coverage check;
5415:   - the system *shall* curate the infra-class list by incident and re-justify it at milestones.
5416:3. *when* a full run completes, the system *shall* read its own wall-time against the architecture's stated number and red on an overrun naming both figures. [INV-41, INV-164]
5417:
5418:**Case: the classes are the host's to declare**
5419:
5420:4. The system *shall* read the reach map's directory classes from `guardrails.config.json` under a `reach_classes` key, the same layers the host's `project.layers` already carries. [INV-224, INV-135]
5421:5. *if* the config names no classes, *then* the system *shall* leave every changed file unclassified and run the full suite on every push. [INV-224]
5422:
5423:**Case: the cheap gates never scope**
5424:
5425:6. The system *shall* run the prover-record, ownership, coverage, loadability, and prototype-fence checks at every push that carries content, except a deletion-only push (criterion 7); an inbox-deposit push under inbox/; or a push in the owner's recordless class — docs/prover/, docs/skill-review/, docs/language-reads/. [INV-40]
5426:
5427:**Case: a deletion-only push carries no content**
5428:
5429:7. *when* every ref-update line git feeds the pre-push hook carries the all-zero local object id, the system *shall* read the push as deletion-only and *shall* stand the whole gate chain down. [INV-290]
5430:8. *when* the chain stands down for a deletion-only push, the system *shall* print one line naming the stand-down and its reason, deriving no reach and running no suite. [INV-290]
5431:9. *when* at least one fed line carries a real object id, the system *shall* run the push gate exactly as on any other push, never reading a mixed push as deletion-only. [INV-290]
5432:10. *if* the hook reads no ref-update lines, *then* the system *shall* run the whole gate chain as an ordinary push, since an unreadable input names no deletion to stand down for. [INV-290]
5433:
5434:---
5435:
5436:## Requirement 227: A blocking gate speaks one typed language
5437:
5438:**Context:** Today each gate script fails in its own words, so an agent parses prose and a human hunts for the fix. Every blocking gate instead emits, on red, one parseable failure object beside its human-readable lines, and every check declares itself blocking or advisory.
5439:
5440:**User Story:** As an agent or a person reading a red gate, I want each blocking gate to emit one typed failure line carrying the fix, so that the reason and the remedy are read the same way from every gate.

6546:
6547:## Requirement 272: A law that earns a gate gets a retroactive gate over the whole tree
6548:
6549:**Context:** When a request or a stated law is extracted into a mechanical gate, the gate's scan is retroactive by construction: it reads the entire tracked tree, or the whole gated artifact set, rather than the changed lines alone. So the debt that predates the gate is found the day the gate lands, never the day each old file happens to be touched next.
6550:
6551:**User Story:** As a person landing a new gate, I want its scan to read the whole tree from the first landing, so that debt older than the gate is found at once, in a single sweep of the tree.
6552:
6553:### Acceptance Criteria
6554:
6555:**Case: the scan is retroactive by construction**
6556:
6557:1. *when* a law is extracted into a mechanical gate, the system *shall* scan the entire tracked tree or the whole gated artifact set, reaching beyond the changed lines, so debt that predates the gate is found the day the gate lands, as the browser-mute gate reds an old script the same as a new one. [INV-176, INV-164, INV-157]
6558:
6559:**Case: an over-big backlog and the catch-up run**
6560:
6561:2. *when* the found backlog is too big to fold at once, the system *shall* absorb it by the seeding law, seeding the cap at the current size so it ratchets down. [INV-176, INV-172]
6562:3. *when* adoption or a catch-up walk runs, the system *shall* run the pack's current gate set backward over the host's existing tree the same way. [INV-176, A-11]

6566:## Requirement 273: The pack's version is one fact, stamped outward from one home
6567:
6568:**Context:** The product's version lives in one place, the root VERSION file. Every skill's frontmatter version line and every in-text base-version reference is a stamped copy written by the sync script at every bump and held by a guard test, so a copy that drifts reds the guard test instead of quietly disagreeing. A per-skill number hand-rolled at edit time drifts the moment attention does.
6569:
6570:**User Story:** As a maintainer reading a version anywhere in the pack, I want every shown version to be a stamped copy of one root home, so that no two copies can disagree and a record's version line names the pack version.

docs/attic/2026-07-22-pre-format/PRODUCT_SPEC.md:702:**A test is green only when it passes deterministically, and a flaky test whose root is in owned code is a defect fixed at that root.** A test is green only when it passes for the same reason on every run. A test that passes on some runs and fails on others is flaky, and one question routes the flake: is the source of the nondeterminism removable in code the project owns, the test or the product? When it is — a dependence on wall-clock time, on test ordering, on shared or leaked state, on an unseeded random draw, on a timing or animation assumption, or a missing wait on an external tool the test drives — the flake is a defect fixed at that root, the source named and removed, so the test passes every run for the same reason. It is masked by nothing: no retry, no rerun-until-green, no raised timeout that hides the race, and no "it passed this time" accepted as a pass. When the nondeterminism is not removable in owned code, because the external tool itself misbehaves at random with nothing to correct in the test, it is workshop noise on the problem ledger [INV-23], a separate home. The seam question — removable in owned code — decides which home, so an owned defect never drifts into the ledger, where a second occurrence could otherwise be tolerated as an agreed non-problem [INV-9], the permanent toleration this law exists to forbid. The enforcement is two nets: a mechanical gate greps the test configuration for a retry or rerun-until-green plugin and reds when one appears, because that mask is deterministically detectable; the rest is the verify walk's discipline, the same kind of net as the fresh-eyes audit [INV-46]. Where the root is not yet found, a bounded read of the test and its inputs finds it before any fix, because the good infrastructure fix comes first. A flake whose root is understood but not removable in one landing is quarantined by name in the pinned skip-set, marked as a quarantined flake distinct from an environment skip, with a dated reason and an owning queue row [INV-80, INV-70]; an open quarantine holds no landing and stands as a debt the milestone audit reads [INV-145]. The green definition at build-pipeline's verify step and the test-author skill both carry it: green means deterministic. [INV-155]

262:`bash <pack>/adopt/install-ratchet.sh` from the host root (SPEC INV-172). It vendors the scripts

264:at once, shrinking-only from then on — and generates the guard test. The section below covers the
265:structural gates, which are adapted by hand.

267:The gate shape (fresh review · green tests · ownership · full coverage · prototype fence ·
268:loadability · pin drift · host checks · shipped language · no broad kill · freeze · muted launch ·
269:config health) is the part worth copying as-is. What changes per host:
270:
271:- **Test command.** Swap `python3 -m pytest -q tests` in `check-tests.sh` for whatever the host
272:  runs (`npm test`, `go test`, …) — and set the CI mirror to the SAME command, so the local net
273:  never under-runs what CI runs (a runner that collects fewer tests than CI false-greens locally).
274:- **Review cadence.** Not every host proves the whole spec before every push — a host may
275:  only require a full prover pass before a major version, checking something lighter
276:  (or nothing) in between. That cadence is a host setting; state it in
277:  the host's own profile and adjust `check-prover-record.sh`'s expectations (or drop gate a
278:  entirely) to match.

280:  it as the script's argument, or edit the default.

282:  `prototype/` (say `sketches/` or `labs/`), pass that name as
283:  `check-prototype-fence.sh`'s second argument instead of renaming the script.

content.text:
# Findings

## Bottom line

**There is no documented bypass for either failure class as a *procedure of the push road*.** Nothing in the spec, the skills, `docs/push-law.md`, or `guardrails/README.md` describes an env-var carve-out, an owner-word exemption, or a `--no-verify` road for gate m skill-drift or the worker-restore transcript gate.

What *is* written down is narrower and must not be conflated:

| Situation | Written-down thing | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| gate m, **hook** drift | `guardrails/local-overrides.json` declared override | (a) a real, spec'd data mechanism — **but hooks only** |
| gate m, **skill** drift | `scripts/sync-skills.sh` — the one named fix | (a) a repair, not a bypass. **No override mechanism exists** |
| gate b, worker-restore red | move `COUNTING_FROM` forward on a *recorded* finding | (a) a written repair law in the gate's own header — not a push bypass |
| pushing anyway | `git push --no-verify` after running `bash guardrails/pre-push` yourself | (a) written, but in `NEXT_STEPS.md` only, and as a **cost-saving habit on a green verdict**, not a red-tolerating road |

---

## 1. `guardrails/pre-push` — every stand-down, skip, and early exit (full read, 286 lines)

`/private/tmp/live-spec-integrate-slimdown/wt/guardrails/pre-push`

**The script honours no environment variable of its own.** There is no `LIVE_SPEC_*`, no `SKIP_*`, no `FORCE`, no override flag anywhere in the file. Grep for env references returns only `$REPO_ROOT`, `$GUARDRAILS`, `$PUSH_REF_LINES` (read from stdin) and `SCOPED_TEST_FILES` (set *by* the script).

Exactly three things make it stand down or exit early:

**a. Deletion-only stand-down — the only early `exit 0`** (lines 30–47):
```
30:# STAND-DOWN: deletion-only
31:if [ -t 0 ]; then
...
44:    echo "PUSH ALLOWED — deletion-only push: standing the full gate chain down ..."
45:    exit 0
```
Fires only when every ref-update line git feeds on stdin carries the all-zero object id. Note line 31: a manual invocation (`bash guardrails/pre-push`, tty stdin) sets `PUSH_REF_LINES=""` and therefore **cannot** trigger it.

**b. gate b scoping by reach verdict** (lines 73–89):
```
76:    echo "   prose-only diff: the suite stands down by name; every other gate still runs."
```
`reach_code` 0 = prose-only (suite skipped), 2 = scoped (subset of test files), anything else = full suite. Set by `guardrails/check-push-reach.sh`, not by any env var. A change to `skills/*/SKILL.md` is not prose-only in the sense that skips the suite here — and in any case gate m is unaffected: "every other gate still runs."

**c. gate n is report-only** (lines 185–193) — the inbox earned-message check never blocks. Irrelevant to your two gates.

Everything else — including gate m at line 172 and gate b at line 73 — sets `fail=1` and ends at:
```
266:  echo "PUSH BLOCKED — one or more gates above failed. Fix them and try again."
267:  exit 1
```

**Carve-outs living in the child scripts** (these do exist, and they are the only env-sensitive doors):
- `guardrails/check-config-health.sh:14-17` — `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` or `CI=true` skips the **whole** gate-m script, by name. Spec'd at `PRODUCT_SPEC.md:6519` (R270.4) and `:6543` (R271.4) as the CI-checkout carve-out.
- `guardrails/check-prover-record.sh:107` and `check-skill-review.sh:55` — `LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE` moves the diff base (CI passes `github.event.before`).
- `guardrails/check-tests.sh:78` — `LIVE_SPEC_SCRATCH` marks a scratch copy.
- `guardrails/check-worker-restore.py:917,924` — `LIVE_SPEC_TRANSCRIPT_ROOT` and `LIVE_SPEC_WORKER_RESTORE_FROM`.

**I must flag this sharply:** setting `CI=true` locally would silence gate m, and `LIVE_SPEC_TRANSCRIPT_ROOT=/nonexistent` would make the worker-restore gate stand down. **Neither is documented anywhere as a push procedure.** These are things I deduce are technically possible. The repo's own language treats the CI variable as a *checkout property*, not a switch ("a CI checkout installs no local hooks by design"), and treats the transcript root as a relocation flag for reading history (`guardrails/README.md:213`). The root directory of the worktree contains a stray `nonexistent-ci-home/` (created 19:25 today) which suggests a fresh-HOME probe was run — see §4.

---

## 2. Gate m / config-health: the documented paths

`guardrails/check-config-health.sh` has **three** arms, and only one of them has an override.

**Hook arm (lines 61–87) — has a declared-override mechanism:**
```
62:      # A machine may deliberately run a changed copy of a hook — a check switched off for a stated
63:      # span while the documents it reads are rewritten, say. The repository stays the version
64:      # everyone gets, and the difference is declared as DATA in guardrails/local-overrides.json
65:      # rather than by editing this script. An entry pins the fingerprint of the installed file it
66:      # covers, so it buys silence for exactly that copy: change the installed file again and the
67:      # entry stops matching and this arm reds. An undeclared difference still reds (2026-08-04).
```
Entry shape required (lines 76–79): `hook` + `installed_sha256` + a non-empty `reason`. Live examples with `added`/`review_by` dates at `guardrails/local-overrides.json:4-17`. The remedy is stated in the red itself (line 84): *"run scripts/install-pack-hooks.sh or scripts/install-session-hooks.sh, or declare the difference in guardrails/local-overrides.json with its reason and the installed file's fingerprint."* A worked instance of a worker choosing between the two is at `docs/prover/2026-08-11-thirty-commit-range.md:69`.

**Skill arm (lines 101–122) — no override exists.** The code path is:
```
118:      echo "{... \"message\":\"installed skill drifted from source: $sname\",\"fix\":\"run scripts/sync-skills.sh\"}"
119:      fail=1
```
`local-overrides.json` is **not consulted** in this loop — the JSON key is `hook_overrides` and it is read only inside the hook arm. The only exemption in the skill arm is the external-skill fence (line 110: a skill dir carrying its own `.git` is skipped).

The spec confirms one fix and no override:
- `PRODUCT_SPEC.md:6537` (R271.1): *"when an installed skill tree is un-synced or drifted against the pack's `skills/` source, the system shall red the config-health check's skill-copy arm and name the one fix, to re-run `scripts/sync-skills.sh`."*
- `PRODUCT_SPEC.md:6542` (R271.3): the shipped skill's installed copy is held **byte-pristine**; even an extra file inside counts as drift.

## 5. The "machine-local failures" class — recognised, but never given a bypass

The class has a name and is repeatedly tolerated in prover records, always on the owner's word and always as *the record's own judgment*, never as a standing rule:

- `docs/prover/2026-08-14-push-review.md:70` — *"The full suite at b2fc1af fails four host-local checks on the review machine. A fresh-HOME probe with the CI variables set passes all three underlying checks. Expected CI result on this push: green."*
- `docs/prover/2026-08-14-push-review-2.md:13` — *"The four tolerated machine-local failures and the certification road are unchanged from docs/prover/2026-08-14-push-review.md."*
- `docs/prover/2026-08-16-integration-push.md:42` — *"The owner's conditional word of 2026-08-15 23:11 authorizes this push: the verdict line reads ALLOW-WITH-NOTES and the suite carries zero failures beyond the four machine-local checks..."*

Important caveats on this evidence:
1. The "four machine-local checks" are **never enumerated in any file I could find**. There is no roster, no JSON declaration, no spec clause. It is a phrase used inside dated prover records.
2. "the certification road" is referenced at `2026-08-14-push-review-2.md:13` as if it were a named procedure, but **the only text it points to is `2026-08-14-push-review.md:70`**, which is one paragraph describing a fresh-HOME probe. There is no document defining a certification road.
3. Every one of these pushes ran under an explicitly dated owner authorization recorded in the record's own Execution note. That is the mechanism actually in use: **a dated owner word, written into the prover record, per push.** It is not a standing carve-out, and it is not the worker's to grant.

The pattern is closest to what you'd call an owner-word exemption, but it is (a) a recorded per-push judgment, not (b) a documented standing procedure a worker can invoke.
